runs.driving_observable: DE-ESCALATED AMBER -> GREEN — both legs of the written de-escalation test resolved, one terminally closed and one exceeded. (1) FILING LEG CLOSED: the Section 16 deadline for unlock-day (08-06) transactions was end of Monday 08-10; the SPCX submissions feed (data.sec.gov, checked today) shows ZERO Form 4s since the single known 06-17 filing — through the unlock and the entire following week, no Section 16 person reported any disposition. Per the 08-07 structural note a quiet tape confirms only weakly (Form 4 covers ~10 people, not the 911.5M rank-and-file shares), so the tape alone would not support GREEN — but the tape is no longer alone. (2) PRICE LEG EXCEEDED: the clause required price to hold above $105.11 through the following week; the week instead delivered absorption-plus-re-rating — five sessions at 108.9M-242.1M volume, closes $133.11 / $138.74 / $133.29 / $146.15 / $141.29, re-crossing the $135 IPO offer, volume decaying from 2.0x average to ~1.0x today. A doubled float (4.9% -> 11.8%) met demand exceeding supply for a full week: whatever rank-and-file selling occurred was realized INTO that demand without price damage — which is the 'modest realized selling' the clause was written to detect, evidenced by outcome where filings are structurally silent. Run dynamics require strategic complementarity in selling; the observed dynamics (index/passive accumulation, reported short-covering, re-rating above the offer) are its opposite. CORROBORATING, WEAK: two routine Rule 13d-1(d) Schedule 13Gs (Musk, Gracias/Valor) confirm baseline holdings as-of 06-30 unchanged from the 424B4 — pre-unlock snapshots, not unlock behavior. CAVEATS CARRIED FORWARD: the short-covering leg of the rally is borrowed demand; structural run capacity is unchanged (float 11.8%, staggered tranches through the 2026-12-08 full expiry); and ~425M locked shares arrive at the Cursor close.

The uncollared Cursor issuance is repricing in SPCX's favor: at ~$141 the fixed $60B consideration is ~425M shares vs 444.4M at the offer and 522.1M at the 08-06 close — the recovery retired ~97M shares of contingent dilution in one week. Press of 08-12/08-13 (SatNews; Seeking Alpha citing Cursor; CNBC) reports regulatory procedures finalizing with closing expected within days and by end-August at the latest — meaning the 7-trading-day VWAP window that mechanically fixes the count is effectively running NOW on $133-146 prints. NOT moved to GREEN on two closes: the recovery is 2 sessions old against a full sub-offer record, and the terminal event is days away anyway — closing extinguishes the $10B/$4B cash termination exposure entirely (fees are payable only on termination) and converts the uncollared obligation into a fixed, already-locked share count. PRIOR BASIS RETAINED: pledge channel ruled out (2,618,530 shares total, immaterial at any trigger price); termination fees cash-only for a public Parent (11.04(d)), split 15/85 termination/deferred-services (11.04(f)); the Compute Agreement and its Annex A remain unfiled — a permanent observability limit; company secured debt asset-backed, not stock-backed.

observables.cursor_acq_stock_component: ~$60B all-stock, consideration formula now filing-verified (EX-10.1 Section 1.01): Exchange Ratio = Company Implied Per Share Value / Parent Share Price, where Company Implied Per Share Value = a FIXED $60,000,000,000 equity value divided by Anysphere's fully diluted capitalisation, and Parent Share Price = the volume-weighted average closing price over the 7 consecutive trading days ending the trading day immediately preceding Closing. NO COLLAR: Section 2.05 adjusts only for reclassification, split, recap and stock-dividend events, with no floor, ceiling or price-based walk-away. Issuance therefore scales as 1/P without bound — 444.4M shares at $135, 522.1M at $114.92, 570.8M at $105.11, 666.7M at $90, 800.0M at $75 (3.37% / 3.96% / 4.33% / 5.06% / 6.07% of shares outstanding); each 10% decline issues 11.1% more stock. Shares issued carry a Lock-Up Period (Letter of Transmittal; Exhibit D IPO Lock-Up Agreement), so they do not enter float at closing. Expected close Q3 2026 under antitrust scrutiny. Termination fees $10B (Total Fee) / $4B (Regulatory Total Fee), never both (11.04(e)), and payable ONLY IN CASH now that Parent is public (11.04(d)); the $10B fee is further conditioned on the separate SPCX-Anysphere Compute Agreement. FEE STRUCTURE REFINED FROM PRIMARY FILINGS — the $10B is mostly NOT a break fee. Merger agreement Section 11.04(f), tracking Section 6.2(b) of the Compute Agreement, splits it 15/85, and the 424B4 states the split in plain numbers: $1.5B termination fee under the option/merger agreement PLUS $8.5B deferred services fee under the separate Compute Agreement. The same 15/85 split applies to the $4B regulatory fee ($0.6B + $3.4B). These are different legal animals: a break fee is liquidated damages on a transaction that did not happen; a deferred services fee is consideration under a commercial contract that did. Deal history also corrected: the acquisition was never a commitment but a CALL OPTION dated 2026-04-19, exercisable in the 30-day window following the earlier of (i) seven trading days after IPO completion and (ii) 2026-09-30, at SPCX's sole discretion with board approval, with Cursor under exclusivity; the 10-Q carries its initial fair value at ZERO. SPCX exercised in June and signed the merger agreement 06-16. Cash-only settlement confirmed from a second document: the 424B4 says the fees are "payable in cash (or Class A common stock, if this offering has not been consummated at the time the fees become payable)" — the IPO closed 06-12, so the stock election lapsed. UPDATE 08-13: regulatory procedures reported finalizing (SatNews 08-12; Seeking Alpha: Cursor says deal could be done by end of the week of 08-10; multiple outlets: end-August at the latest). At the $141.29 close the consideration is ~425.4M shares (~3.23% of outstanding) vs 522.1M at the 08-06 close. No closing 8-K on EDGAR as of 08-13 — the 06-26 8-K is still the latest.

observables.counterparty_web_status: CORRECTED — xAI IS NOT A COUNTERPARTY, IT IS INSIDE SPCX. SpaceX acquired X.AI Holdings Corp. effective 2026-02-02 (the "xAI Merger"); xAI had itself acquired X Holdings effective 2025-03-28. Both were common-control transactions and the financials are retrospectively recast (424B4, Basis of Presentation). The prospectus defines the AI segment as the business "acquired in connection with our acquisition of xAI in February 2026… includes our AI compute, Grok, and X". Every prior entry treating xAI as an external node checked for operational distress was wrong: xAI stress is DIRECT SEGMENT EXPOSURE, not contagion. The distinction is load-bearing in a Brunnermeier-Reis frame — network transmission has lags and possible circuit-breakers, balance-sheet exposure has neither. Also newly recorded: the same filing shows a five-for-one stock split effective 2026-05-04, which is why all share figures are retroactively adjusted. REVISED WEB: (i) Cursor/Anysphere — dual-role, both a compute counterparty since 2026-04-19 and the pending acquisition target, closing expected Q3 2026 under antitrust scrutiny; (ii) the Valor SPV — ALSO dual-role, since the Valor entities hold ~503.4M shares (7.3% pre-offering) through Antonio J. Gracias, who is a director, making the compute-SPV counterparty simultaneously a large shareholder and board-connected; (iii) Anthropic as a compute customer; (iv) Mesh Optical, acquired and closed 2026-07-06, now internal. No node is in visible operational distress. The genuine external web is therefore SMALLER than previously recorded, and two of its three remaining nodes are dual-role — which concentrates rather than diversifies the exposure. UPDATE 08-13: Cursor node strengthening — regulatory procedures reported finalizing, close expected by end-August; on closing, Cursor moves from external dual-role node to internal segment (as Mesh Optical did 07-06), shrinking the external web to Valor and Anthropic-as-customer.
